description: Known disagreements between kmc-package's checkForDuplicatedOrNonMinimalLanguages (CLDR Intl.Locale.minimize) and the studio's isWellFormedBcp47 + minimalTagOf (pinned langtags), over every .kps <Language ID> in ../keyboards. One record per (kind, tag) per keyboard, carrying BOTH sides' verdicts ('none' when a side found nothing). The parity test fails on any disagreement not listed here, any listed disagreement that no longer occurs, and any listed disagreement whose kmc/studio verdict changed. Populated from the first run (spec 115 T060) and re-captured under the pinned Node on 2026-11-14 (see below); each entry carries the reason. Two systematic divergences: CLDR minimize applies language aliases and drops likely subtags (e.g. kgy-Deva -> kgy, mnk -> man, or resolve und -> en), while minimalTagOf never renames a language for CLDR's sake, folds only to langtags' canonical code, drops only the tagset's own defaults, and returns the tagset's registered tag (which can name a default region, e.g. ku-Arab -> ku-Arab-TR). Validity agrees everywhere: no `invalid` disagreement in the corpus. The kmc side is Intl.Locale.minimize, so its verdicts follow the host Node's ICU/CLDR: the first capture was made under Node 24, whose ICU answers ku-Arab -> ku-IQ and dek -> sqm, while the pinned Node (.nvmrc, 22.19.0) answers ku-Arab -> ku-Arab and dek -> dek — the 2026-11-14 re-capture under 22.19.0 corrected the ku, dek, arv, bsq, kgy and mnk rows. Always re-capture under the pinned Node.

disagreements.reason: langtags strips Latn as arv's default script (its tagset's full form is arv-Latn-ET); the pinned Node's CLDR has no likely-subtags entry for arv at all (maximize('arv') is 'arv'), so minimize leaves arv-Latn alone.
CLDR minimize applies the language alias tl -> fil (tl-Tglg -> fil-Tglg); langtags keeps the author's code - minimalTagOf never renames a language.
CLDR minimize collapses fil-Tglg and tl-Tglg to the same minimal tag fil-Tglg; the studio keeps them distinct (its minimal forms differ).

CLDR minimize applies the alias kmr -> ku but keeps the script Arab: ku's likely script is Latn (ku -> ku-Latn-TR), so dropping Arab would change the maximized form (ku-Arab -> ku-Arab-IQ), and minimize never invents a region (kmr-Arab -> ku-Arab); langtags folds kmr to its canonical code ku and returns its registered tag ku-Arab-TR. Both rename the language; they disagree on script and region.

CLDR minimize leaves ku-Arab alone: Arab is not ku's likely script (Latn is — ku -> ku-Latn-TR), so the script is not redundant, and minimize never invents a region; langtags returns its registered tag ku-Arab-TR, which names its default region. CLDR never returns a region the tag did not carry; langtags never drops a registered tag's default region.

Both sides agree ku-Arab and kmr-Arab collapse to one minimal tag, but disagree on the minimal form: CLDR says ku-Arab, langtags says ku-Arab-TR (the same divergence as the non-minimal finding for these tags).
minimalTagOf collapses ku-Arab-TR and kmr-Arab to the same minimal tag ku-Arab-TR; CLDR minimize keeps them distinct.
